items.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb C^4$ with complex-bilinear form $h(p,q)=p^0q^0-p^1q^1-p^2q^2-p^3q^3$. This is $h=-\eta$ for $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, the adopted $(-+++)$ coordinate convention. Coordinates $p^\mu$ have inverse-length units. Let $\mathbb C^2$ and $\widetilde{\mathbb C}^2$ be separate two-dimensional complex vector spaces, with undotted components $\lambda_a$ and dotted components $\widetilde\lambda_{\dot a}$; no complex-conjugation relation is imposed between them.

Define the linear map $\kappa:V\to M_2(\mathbb C)$ by

$$\kappa(p)=p^0I_2+p^1\sigma_1+p^2\sigma_2+p^3\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}p^0+p^3&p^1-ip^2\\p^1+ip^2&p^0-p^3\end{pmatrix},$$

where the dimensionless Pauli matrices are $\sigma_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma_3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Its inverse sends $M=(M_{a\dot a})$ to

$$\kappa^{-1}(M)=\left(\frac{M_{1\dot1}+M_{2\dot2}}2,\frac{M_{1\dot2}+M_{2\dot1}}2,\frac{M_{2\dot1}-M_{1\dot2}}{2i},\frac{M_{1\dot1}-M_{2\dot2}}2\right).$$

For a matrix $M$ whose image is one-dimensional (rank one), a spinor factorization is a pair $(\lambda,\widetilde\lambda)\in(\mathbb C^2\setminus\{0\})\times(\widetilde{\mathbb C}^2\setminus\{0\})$ satisfying $M_{a\dot a}=\lambda_a\widetilde\lambda_{\dot a}$. The associated momentum is $p=\kappa^{-1}(M)$. Spinor factors have units of inverse square-root length, so their outer product has momentum units. A little-group rescaling is $(\lambda,\widetilde\lambda)\mapsto(t\lambda,t^{-1}\widetilde\lambda)$ for dimensionless $t\in\mathbb C^\times$; it leaves $p$ unchanged. On factorization pairs of a fixed $M$, identify pairs related by such a rescaling; the spinor-helicity class of $M$ is an equivalence class for this $\mathbb C^\times$ action.

Set $\epsilon^{12}=1$, $\epsilon^{21}=-1$, and $\epsilon^{11}=\epsilon^{22}=0$, and use a second copy with dotted indices. Raise indices by $\lambda^a=\epsilon^{ab}\lambda_b$ and $\widetilde\lambda^{\dot a}=\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\widetilde\lambda_{\dot b}$. Define angle and square brackets by $\langle\lambda r\rangle=\epsilon^{ab}\lambda_a r_b$ and $[\widetilde\lambda\widetilde r]=\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\widetilde\lambda_{\dot a}\widetilde r_{\dot b}$.

For $n\ge1$ and assigned half-integer helicity labels $h_1,\ldots,h_n\in\tfrac12\mathbb Z$, an outgoing helicity-$h_i$ amplitude on a domain $D$ of $n$ spinor-factorization data is a function $A_n:D\to\mathbb C$. Require $D$ to be invariant under independent little-group rescalings. The amplitude condition is, for each leg $i$ and each admissible $t\in\mathbb C^\times$,

$$A_n(\ldots,t\lambda_i,t^{-1}\widetilde\lambda_i,\ldots)=t^{-2h_i}A_n(\ldots,\lambda_i,\widetilde\lambda_i,\ldots).$$

This definition imposes no rationality, factorization, or physical scattering assumption. The next item proves that every nonzero momentum $p$ with $h(p,p)=0$ has a spinor factorization, unique up to the stated rescaling.

items.statement: For every $p\in\mathbb C^4$, $\det\kappa(p)=h(p,p)$. Thus for every nonzero $p$ with $h(p,p)=0$, $\kappa(p)$ has a spinor factorization. If $\kappa(p)_{a\dot a}=\lambda_a\widetilde\lambda_{\dot a}=\lambda'_a\widetilde\lambda'_{\dot a}$, then there is a unique $t\in\mathbb C^\times$ such that $\lambda'=t\lambda$ and $\widetilde\lambda'=t^{-1}\widetilde\lambda$. Hence the spinor-helicity class of each nonzero null momentum is nonempty and has one element.

items.statement:
Let $n\ge4$ and let $p_1,\ldots,p_n\in\mathbb C^4\setminus\{0\}$ be complex null momenta with $\sum_{a=1}^n p_a=0$. Choose spinor factors $\kappa(p_a)=\lambda_a\widetilde\lambda_a$, whose existence is established by the null-factorization result on this page, and choose distinct labels $i,j$. The spinor factors and $h$ use the convention in the spinor-helicity definition. For dimensionless $z\in\mathbb C$, make the two-line shift

$$\lambda_i(z)=\lambda_i+z\lambda_j,\qquad \widetilde\lambda_j(z)=\widetilde\lambda_j-z\widetilde\lambda_i,$$

leaving $\widetilde\lambda_i$, $\lambda_j$ and every other spinor unchanged; set $p_a(z)=\kappa^{-1}(\lambda_a(z)\widetilde\lambda_a(z))$.

Let $A(z)=F(z)/G(z)$, where $F,G\in\mathbb C[z]$, $G\not\equiv0$, and common factors are canceled. A finite pole is a zero of the reduced denominator $G$; it is simple when that zero has multiplicity one. Assume $A$ is regular at $z=0$, has distinct simple finite poles $z_1,\ldots,z_m\ne0$ and no other finite poles, and $A(z)\to0$ as $z\to\infty$. For a simple pole, define $r_\alpha=\operatorname{Res}_{z=z_\alpha}A(z)$ as the coefficient of $(z-z_\alpha)^{-1}$ in its Laurent expansion. Then

$$A(0)=-\sum_{\alpha=1}^m\frac{r_\alpha}{z_\alpha}=-\sum_{\alpha=1}^m\operatorname{Res}_{z=z_\alpha}\frac{A(z)}{z}.$$

For a factorization channel, choose a subset $S_\alpha\subset\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $2\le|S_\alpha|\le n-2$, containing exactly one of $i,j$. Put $P_\alpha(z)=\sum_{a\in S_\alpha}p_a(z)$ and $Q_\alpha(z)=h(P_\alpha(z),P_\alpha(z))$. Assume every pole is assigned a distinct such channel with $Q_\alpha(z_\alpha)=0$ and $Q'_\alpha(z_\alpha)\ne0$. Since $z$ is dimensionless, $Q'_\alpha$ has the same inverse-length-squared units as $Q_\alpha$. If the residue factorization

$$r_\alpha=\frac{\displaystyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal H_\alpha}A_{L,s}(z_\alpha)A_{R,-s}(z_\alpha)}{Q'_\alpha(z_\alpha)}$$

holds, where $\mathcal H_\alpha$ is the finite set of internal helicity labels and $A_{L,s},A_{R,-s}$ are the supplied complex values for the two lower-point channel subproblems at the shifted factorization kinematics, with the internal momenta $P_\alpha(z_\alpha)$ and $-P_\alpha(z_\alpha)$ null, then

$$A(0)=-\sum_{\alpha=1}^m\frac{1}{z_\alpha Q'_\alpha(z_\alpha)}\sum_{s\in\mathcal H_\alpha}A_{L,s}(z_\alpha)A_{R,-s}(z_\alpha).$$

This is the BCFW recursion for the stated shift. The residue-factorization equality and the vanishing at infinity are hypotheses here; this theorem does not derive them for a chosen QFT model.

items.title: Reference-spinor changes are pure gauge

references.title: Henriette Elvang and Yu-tin Huang, Scattering Amplitudes
references.locator: §2.4 and the Schouten identity in §2.3, PDF pp. 16–18; massless-vector reference spinors, pure-momentum shifts and the conditional Ward contraction.

references.title: Ruth Britto, Freddy Cachazo, Bo Feng, and Edward Witten, Direct Proof of Tree-Level Recursion Relation in Yang-Mills Theory
references.locator: §3.1, PDF pp. 7–8; spinor-helicity polarization vectors with fixed reference spinors. The local proof establishes the reference difference directly.

items.statement:
Let $p\ne0$ be a complex null momentum and choose its spinor factorization $\kappa(p)_{a\dot a}=\lambda_a\widetilde\lambda_{\dot a}$, which exists by the null-factorization result on this page. Raise spinor indices and define brackets as in the spinor-helicity definition. For an undotted reference spinor $r$ with $\langle\lambda r\rangle\ne0$ and a dotted reference spinor $\widetilde r$ with $[\widetilde\lambda\widetilde r]\ne0$, define polarization tensors

$$E_+^{a\dot a}(p;r)=\sqrt2\,\frac{r^a\widetilde\lambda^{\dot a}}{\langle\lambda r\rangle},\qquad E_-^{a\dot a}(p;\widetilde r)=\sqrt2\,\frac{\lambda^a\widetilde r^{\dot a}}{[\widetilde\lambda\widetilde r]}.$$

The reference spinors have the same inverse-square-root length units as $\lambda$ and $\widetilde\lambda$, so these polarization tensors are dimensionless.

Associate a vector $\varepsilon_\pm^\mu$ to each tensor by the inverse of the raised-index Pauli map $p\mapsto\epsilon^{ab}\epsilon^{\dot a\dot b}\kappa(p)_{b\dot b}$. A polarization change is called pure gauge here when its vector difference is a scalar multiple of $p^\mu$. For any two admissible references of the corresponding chirality, the polarization-vector difference is pure gauge. Therefore, for every complex current $J\in\mathbb C^4$ satisfying the explicitly defined conservation condition $h(p,J)=0$, the contraction $h(\varepsilon_\pm(p;r),J)$ is independent of the reference spinor. Current conservation is a separate hypothesis; no general QFT Ward identity is asserted.
